prompt: Write a retry helper that takes the work as a Supplier lambda and the success condition as a Predicate: retry re-runs an action that throws or returns an unacceptable value, and firstAccepted walks a list of alternative suppliers.
explanation: Passing the work as a Supplier<T> and the success test as a Predicate<T> lets one loop serve any kind of task, because the caller supplies both halves as lambdas at the call site. The try/catch lives inside the loop so a RuntimeException ends only that attempt, not the whole method -- putting it outside the loop would abandon the retries. Counting attempts with a captured int[] in the tests is the usual trick for observing a lambda's side effects, since a lambda cannot assign to a plain captured local.
hints: A plain for loop from 0 to maxAttempts handles the zero and negative cases for free -- the body simply never runs.
Put try { T result = action.get(); if (accept.test(result)) return result; } catch (RuntimeException e) { } INSIDE the loop.
firstAccepted is the same body with a for-each over the suppliers instead of a counter.
